```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "The goal is a first paying customer within 90 days, and Idea A has the lower-friction path to one. It is a B2C purchase at $8–$24/mo, anchored to sourced live price points (Kickresume, WeGoUp). Idea B needs an engineering lead to grant pipeline access, and its own brief says that triggers a DPA and security review.",
    "Idea B's case against undercuts the 90-day window directly. Its sources say buyers must trust the tool never to let a real failure through. The brief says that trust 'typically requires months of track record plus deep CI telemetry integration', and new installs face a cold-start problem with no historical data.",
    "Idea A cites concrete, sourced acquisition costs: Meta lead ads at about $12.30 per lead, and Google CPL at $117.92 in 2024, falling about 46.7% in 2025. A solo operator could start paid tests immediately. Idea B's main channel is founder-time content marketing, whose low cost is marked [unsourced]. Its self-serve listing is the GitHub Marketplace, and the brief cites no traction or conversion data for that channel.",
    "Idea A's MVP is a bounded text-LLM pipeline (parse, identify gaps, generate roadmap) with no third-party system integration. Idea B's six-week MVP claim is explicitly [unsourced], so it counts as missing. Idea B also needs per-CI-platform integration work the brief cannot size.",
    "Both ideas face crowded fields with free alternatives. Idea B's field adds funded incumbents (Develocity, Harness, BrowserStack) and an enterprise-skewed, contact-sales pricing norm. That makes a quick self-serve first sale less likely than in Idea A's consumer market."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "Idea B's demand evidence. Its lead quote comes from a TLM at Trunk, itself a flaky-test vendor, describing an internal dashboard. That is not independent evidence that teams will pay a third party for an LLM-based gating tool. The Reddit quote praises sorting and ticketing features, not LLM test selection. Combined with the [unsourced] six-week MVP claim, the brief has no evidence that small or mid-sized teams will pay for a hosted version over the free OSS options it lists.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate-low confidence. Idea A has serious, well-documented weaknesses. Several free direct competitors exist. The need is one-time, which caps lifetime value. Free-to-paid conversion is unverified, and the figures cited are cost per lead, not cost per paying customer. The sensitive gap reasons (health, caregiving) add harm risk. Its demand quotes show anxiety, and the ChatGPT quote also suggests users may substitute a general chatbot. Idea A wins mainly because a single low-priced B2C sale is more reachable in 90 days than earning gating trust and passing security review in Idea B. Neither brief shows sourced evidence of willingness to pay for this specific product."
}
```
